subject: Urgent: Starlift throughput degradation — exec cadence & customer updates
messages:
From: Emily Barnes <emily.barnes@starlift.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput drop this morning (prod)

Vanessa / team,

We started seeing a significant drop in inference throughput in our production environment around 08:40 PT this morning. P95 latency also spiked above our SLO and a handful of requests returned 500s. The pattern looks like sustained reduced tokens/sec across several routes.

Attached is an extract of the last hour (starlift_metrics_20260406.csv). Can you confirm if this is on Redwood's side or if there's anything we should change in our client configuration? This is causing failures in our payment pipeline, so we need an ETA.

Thanks,
Emily Barnes
Director, Platform Ops — Starlift AI
[attachment: starlift_metrics_20260406.csv (csv)]
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Barnes <emily.barnes@starlift.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop this morning (prod)

Emily — thank you for the data and the heads up.

Quick update: I've opened an incident (INF-9182) and looped in infra/serving. Marcus and Vivek, can you triage ASAP? Laura, FYI — this has started hitting Starlift payments.

Immediate asks we need from your side to speed triage:
- Confirm whether you deployed any client-side changes between 07:30–08:45 PT.
- Can you share a short list of affected routes (if different from what you attached) and sample request IDs?

As soon as we have kernel-level AM logs and the prefix cache hit ratios we’ll share a timeframe. I’ll set a standing 30-min exec cadence until we stabilize.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden throughput drop this morning (prod)

On it. Preliminary look: we see bursty GPU queue depth and a corresponding drop in KV cache hit rate around 08:35 PT for the Starlift tenant. No obvious autoscaler events. Collecting detailed perf counters (AM/logs + kernel metrics).

Immediate mitigation options we're evaluating:
- Force-roll a warm model replica (same version) to clear degraded node-local cache state.
- Temporarily route critical routes to a higher-capacity pool (will add cost).
- Apply a targeted prefix-cache whitelist to improve hit rate for payment-related prefixes.

I'll post the perf dump and recommendation in the Jira ticket in 20–30 minutes.

—Marcus
Director, Serving Infrastructure
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Barnes <emily.barnes@starlift.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, ops@starlift.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop this morning (prod) — immediate actions and exec cadence

Emily, Tom — quick note to confirm we are actively working this and to propose a short cadence.

What we are doing now:
- Engineering (Marcus) is collecting kernel/perf dumps and will attempt a targeted warm-replica roll at ~10:15 PT.
- We are preparing a temporary routing plan to shift highest-priority payment routes to a larger pool if the roll does not restore throughput.
- I will host a 15-minute exec sync at 11:00 PT and then every 60 minutes until we are back at normal throughput and error rates.

Please expect a status update at 10:30 PT with initial findings. If you can share the three sample request IDs, that would help correlate logs faster.

Best,
Vanessa

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Emily Barnes <emily.barnes@starlift.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 14:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-mitigation status and customer comms

Team / Emily,

Summary (final status):
- Timeline: Incident began ~08:40 PT 2026-04-06. Root cause: node-local cache fragmentation after a background maintenance job + transient eviction pressure during a narrow traffic spike.
- Actions taken: warm-replica roll at 10:16 PT, targeted routing of payment routes to high-capacity pool for 2 hours, and a temporary prefix whitelist.
- Outcome: Throughput restored to pre-incident levels by 11:10 PT. Error rate returned to baseline by 11:38 PT.

Customer comms recommended (short):
- Opening line: thank you for the data and patience; we identified and remediated an infrastructure-level cache fragmentation issue that caused reduced throughput.
- Technical summary: what we observed (latency/500s), root cause (node-local eviction), and mitigations performed (replica roll, routing, prefix policy).
- Preventive next steps: scheduling an infra change to reduce eviction sensitivity (Q2 config rollout), adding an automated health check that will trigger a warm-replica roll, and a shared post-incident report (we'll publish within 48 hours).

Marcus: please attach the perf dump and a 2–3 paragraph explainer for the post-incident report.
Vivek: please create the health-check ticket and link it to INF-9182.
Vanessa: I'll join the customer follow-up call tomorrow at 09:00 PT unless you need me earlier.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
